simple.meaning: שָׁתַל (shâthal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to transplant.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 10 times across Psalms, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Hosea, beginning at Psalms 1:3. Its contexts include mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁתַל (H8362).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שָׁתַל (shâthal) / H8362 is traced through Psalms 1:3, Psalms 92:14, Jeremiah 17:8, Ezekiel 17:8 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water,

timeline.evidenceText: He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water,
They will still produce fruit in old age.
For he will be as a tree planted by the waters,
It was planted in a good soil by many waters, that it might produce branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a good vine.” ’
Yes, behold, being planted, will it prosper? Won’t it utterly wither when the east wind touches it? It will wither in the beds where it grew.” ’ ”

“The Lord Yahweh says: ‘I will also take some of the lofty top of the cedar, and will plant it. I will crop off from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one, and I will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
I will plant it in the mountain of the height of Israel; and it will produce boughs, and bear fruit, and be a good cedar. Birds of every kind will dwell in the shade of its branches.
Now it is planted in the wilderness,
I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place;
